question.prompt: Two lines intersect. One angle is \(40^\circ\) greater than its adjacent supplementary angle. What is the measure of this angle in degrees?

solutions.explanation: Let this angle be \(x^\circ\). Then \(x-(180-x)=40\), \(2x=220\), and \(x=110\).
solutions.title: Set up a linear equation

solutions.explanation:
The adjacent supplementary angles total \(180^\circ\). Subtracting the larger angle's \(40^\circ\) excess leaves two equal amounts, so the smaller angle is
\[
\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}=70^\circ.
\]
The requested larger angle is therefore \(70^\circ+40^\circ=110^\circ\).
solutions.title: Remove the excess
